clue.text: Woman digesting article about motorway — it's detestable

indicators.note: the enlarged name sits about, that is around, the motorway letter
a woman digesting something takes it inside her, so the article goes into the name

parts.note: Anthea is a woman's name
A is the indefinite article
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Someone detests a woman who reads an article on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema to you is utterly loathed, so 'it's anathema' says it is detestable.

clue.text: But it might not do for the examiner!

definitions.text: But it might not do for the examiner!

parts.words: But it might not do for the examiner!
parts.note: what a candidate writes back to an exam question may be wrong, and so not good enough for the person marking it

explanation.surface: A remark that something may not satisfy an examiner.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply written to an exam question is what the examiner marks, and a poor one will not do.

clue.text: At a distance, say, as an anchor might be

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: something at a distance is away

explanation.surface: Describing an anchor seen from far off.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is described as raised just clear of the sea bed when hauled up, nautical usage for a weighed anchor.

clue.text: Very funny girl's endless evidence of debts

indicators.note: endless means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Hilary is a girl's name
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A girl is very amusing but has run up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarious is a synonym of extremely amusing, causing loud laughter.

clue.text: A couple of residences, one in the City

parts.note: a mansion is one residence
a house is a second residence

explanation.surface: Someone owns two homes, one of them in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, the financial district; Mansion House is the official home of its Lord Mayor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansion House is a single residence located in the City of London, so it is one there.

clue.text: Raised platforms for coaches

definitions.meaning: theatre floors on which actors perform
stagecoaches, horse-drawn passenger carriages, were called this for short

explanation.surface: Elevated platforms built for buses or sports trainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre platforms are stages, and old horse coaches running between stages were also so called.

clue.text: Tom, for example, could do it for a lift

definitions.meaning: Tom ..., the tiny hero of folk tale

definitions.text: could do it for a lift
definitions.meaning: a hitchhiker raises a digit to ask for a ride, using it as a verb

explanation.surface: A man called Tom might help someone get a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb is a folk character, and hitchhikers signal for a ride by sticking out that digit.

clue.text: Eccentric argued pointlessly with advanced student

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters are put in a new order
without a point: E, a compass point, is dropped from the word

parts.note: with means and, joining things

explanation.surface: An odd person argued without point with a senior student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' drops the compass point E from ARGUED, leaving ARGUD, which 'Eccentric' rearranges to GRADU.
explanation.definitionFit: A student about to graduate, having finished the course, is an advanced student awaiting the degree.

clue.text: Act as courier in Ulster, producing confrontation?

parts.note: a courier guiding tourists shows them around
Down is a county in Ulster, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Working as a courier in Northern Ireland leads to a clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive final confrontation is called a showdown, as in a gunfight.

clue.text: Sound Scottish town of first-class quality

indicators.note: sound signals a word spoken the same as the town's name

parts.note: Stirling is a town in central Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish town is praised for being excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the adjective meaning reliable, but it signals a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling describes something of excellent, genuine quality, from the standard of British silver.

clue.text: Rhythmic flexibility presents difficulty at start of opera

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: the start of the word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A problem appears at the beginning of an opera performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is the musical term for freely speeding and slowing tempo, a flexible rhythm.

clue.text: Recuperating porter starts to sip cordial in sisters' place

indicators.note: in places the drink letters inside the nuns' home

parts.note: a convent is where nuns, called sisters, live
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

indicators.note: the starts of the two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A patient recovering takes sips of beer and cordial at the nuns' house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convalescent is recovering health after illness, that is recuperating.

clue.text: Sort of club certain to be' rigorous

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
bound to be means certain to be

explanation.surface: Joining a particular club is sure to be demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironbound means rigid and unyielding, hence rigorous, like something bound in iron.

clue.text: King protected by our new envoy, perhaps? It's possible

indicators.note: the king is guarded on both sides, so it goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps signals the letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is guarded by our newly appointed diplomat, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OUR NEW ENVOY to YOUNEVERNOW; 'protected by' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses that something may well happen; one cannot rule it out.

clue.text: Quality of some birdsong characteristic of marshes

definitions.meaning: a thin, piping tone, like a reed instrument
being full of tall reeds, typical of wetland

explanation.surface: Describing birdsong heard in wetland.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy tone is thin and high, and marshes are reedy, full of reeds; both give the noun.

clue.text: Jockey for position in motocross

definitions.meaning: to struggle or compete hurriedly for a place
a motorcycle race over rough ground

explanation.surface: Riders compete for places in a dirt-bike race.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to compete for position, and a scramble is also a cross-country motorcycle race.

clue.text: Will certain to support defendant's statement

indicators.note: in a down clue, the lower word supports the one above it

parts.note: a plea is what a defendant says, guilty or not guilty
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A will is sure to back up a defendant's claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Will and pleasure are synonyms for desire, as in 'at Her Majesty's pleasure'.

clue.text: Cut joint cooked for earlier meal?

definitions.meaning: to cut someone is to snub them
a joint of meat roasted for a previous meal and now served chilled

explanation.surface: A joint of meat roasted earlier is sliced.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them, and cold shoulder is leftover meat.

clue.text: Scold painter in Spanish port

indicators.note: in puts the painter inside the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A painter is told off in a Spanish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman, a scold.

clue.text: Remain faithful, to Latin woman on illegal drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: ad is Latin for to
her refers to a woman
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Telling a Latin woman on drugs to stay loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause is to stick faithfully to it.

clue.text: It leads to stress, manoeuvring cars in USA

indicators.note: manoeuvring cars moves them around, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Driving cars in America is stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse and music this term means unstressed syllables or notes leading into the first stressed beat.

clue.text: Musteline mammal left with speed

parts.note: speed is rate, as in 'at a rate of knots'

explanation.surface: A weasel-like animal departs quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, belongs to the weasel family, Mustelidae.

clue.text: Losing final directions, papers rejected epic work

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards
losing means those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: dailies are daily newspapers
the last two letters, E and S, are both compass directions

explanation.surface: Newspapers turned down a great poem that lost its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops the final pair from DAILIES to leave DAILI, and 'rejected' turns that round; 'papers' looks like documents but means daily newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem about the Trojan War is a celebrated epic.

clue.text: Man has taken time and energy to evolve

indicators.note: the man has taken in the time, which goes inside

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
an era is a period of time
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man has taken time and effort to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or develop something, the transitive sense of evolve.

clue.text: See archdeacon accommodated in impartial manner

indicators.note: the see houses the archdeacon, taking it inside

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese, a bishop's see
Ven is short for Venerable, an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: Asked to look, an archdeacon is housed fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means fairly, without favouring either side.

clue.text: Instrument closely associated with drums

parts.note: suggests a percussion instrument, but the drums are eardrums, which a doctor's viewing device examines closely

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that goes with the drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The device a doctor uses to examine the ear canal and eardrum is a medical instrument.
